name: Ariel Procaccia
title: Alfred and Rebecca Lin Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on problems related to AI, algorithms, economics, and society, including not-for-profit services for fair division and for selecting citizens' panels by lot, and frameworks for designing new democratic processes.

name: Arjun (Raj) Manrai
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Leads a research lab applying machine learning and statistical modeling to improve medical decision-making. Founding Deputy Editor of NEJM AI and co-host of the NEJM AI Grand Rounds podcast.

name: Bernardo Sabatini
title: Co-director of the Kempner Institute; Alice and Rodman W. Moorhead III Professor of Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Neurobiologist and Howard Hughes Medical Institute Investigator studying how synapses and basal ganglia circuits support action selection, evaluation, and learning. His lab examines how brain plasticity and computation allow animals to adapt to changing contexts.

name: Boaz Barak
title: Catalyst Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on ML foundations, AI safety, cryptography, and computational complexity. As of Fall 2025 he is part-time at Harvard as a Catalyst Professor and part-time a member of the technical staff at OpenAI.

name: Cengiz Pehlevan
title: Associate Professor of Applied Mathematics
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His group investigates how intelligence operates through neural computation, focusing on how computation emerges in neural networks through the collective dynamics of simple processing units, or neurons.

name: Chirag Patel
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops computational and bioinformatics methods to reason over high-throughput data streams spanning molecules to populations. Integrates electronic medical records, environmental exposure measures, and genomic variation to dissect differences in human phenomes.

name: Cynthia Dwork
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Uses theoretical computer science to place societal problems on a firm mathematical foundation, with research spanning theory of computation, machine learning, and computation and society.

name: David Alvarez-Melis
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Data-Centric Machine Learning (DCML) group, studying how data—not just models—shapes the behavior and reliability of AI systems. His work integrates optimal transport, information theory, and generative modeling across scientific, language, and vision domains.

name: David Brooks
title: Haley Family Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research focuses on hardware/software co-design of AI systems, with interests in hardware and software design for computer systems. Professor at Harvard since 2002, previously a Research Staff Member at IBM.

name: David Parkes
title: John A. Paulson Dean of the Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Applies computational methods to economic and social coordination problems, with interests spanning multi-agent AI, bounded rationality, machine learning and decisions, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and mechanism design.

name: Demba Ba
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include computational neuroscience, artificial intelligence, signal processing, and modeling of physical and biological systems.

name: Elena Leah Glassman
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Variation Lab, which designs, builds, and evaluates systems for comprehending and interacting with population-level structure and trends in large code and data corpora, aiming to augment human intelligence.

name: Fernanda Viegas
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Her research areas at Harvard SEAS span machine learning, artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, visualization, and computation and society.

name: Finale Doshi-Velez
title: Herchel Smith Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads Harvard's Data to Actionable Knowledge (DtAK) lab, which uses probabilistic methods to address decision-making scenarios involving humans and AI. Her group focuses on Bayesian models and sequential decision-making from heterogeneous data.

name: Flavio P. Calmon
title: Thomas D. Cabot Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Harvard Information Theory Laboratory, working on information theory, signal processing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, aiming to develop foundational theory that guides the responsible design of ML and AI algorithms.

name: H.T. Kung
title: William H. Gates Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Research in computer architecture, networking, signal processing, machine learning, parallel computing, and security.

name: Haim Sompolinsky
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Molecular and Cellular Biology and of Physics (in Residence)
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Theoretical neuroscientist exploring the foundations of cognitive functions in both biological brains and artificial intelligence systems. Applies principles of statistical mechanics, nonlinear dynamics, disordered systems, and machine learning.

name: Hanspeter Pfister
title: An Wang Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Visual Computing Group, which develops visual analysis tools and methods to help scientists process and understand large multi-dimensional data sets, with recent publications spanning computer vision and video generation.

name: Heng Li
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Studies advanced computational algorithms for practical biological problems, focusing on sequence alignment, variant calling, and de novo assembly. Developed and maintains widely used software packages including BWA, samtools, and minimap2.

name: Hima Lakkaraju
title: Assistant Professor, Harvard Business School; Affiliate in Computer Science
department: Harvard Business School; Affiliate in Computer Science (SEAS)
bio: Researches the algorithmic foundations and societal implications of safe, trustworthy, and responsible AI, developing machine learning and optimization techniques for human and algorithmic decision-making in high-stakes domains such as health care, policy, law, and business.

name: Isaac Kohane
title: Chair of the Department of Biomedical Informatics; Marion V. Nelson Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Inaugural Chair of DBMI who develops and applies computational techniques to address disease at multiple scales, from healthcare systems as living laboratories to the functional genomics of neurodevelopment with a focus on autism. Editor-in-Chief of NEJM AI.

name: Jonathan Frankle
title: Associate in Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences

name: Kanaka Rajan
title: Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Associate Professor of Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Computational neuroscientist studying how cognitive functions such as learning, remembering, and deciding emerge from multi-scale neural processes. Applies frameworks from machine learning and statistical physics to bridge neurobiology and artificial intelligence.

name: Kianté Brantley
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Assistant Professor at the Kempner Institute and SEAS whose research focuses on problems at the intersection of machine learning and natural language processing. His group works on applied reinforcement learning, NLP, and deep learning.

name: Krzysztof Z Gajos
title: Yahn W. Bernier and N. Elizabeth McCaw Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Intelligent Interactive Systems Group at Harvard and is a member of the Center for Human-driven AI Research and Methods (CHARM). His interests include principles and applications of intelligent interactive systems.

name: Kun-Hsing Yu
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Integrates quantitative histopathology image patterns with multi-omics profiles to advance cancer research and clinical practice. His team develops fully-automated algorithms to analyze whole-slide histopathology images at scale.

name: Leslie G. Valiant
title: T. Jefferson Coolidge Professor of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research spans theory of computation, machine learning, computational neuroscience, and artificial intelligence, including work on neuroidal architectures for cognitive computation and the book Circuits of the Mind.

name: Lucas B Janson
title: Associate Professor of Statistics; Affiliate in Computer Science
bio: Studies high-dimensional inference and statistical machine learning, collaborating with domain experts in genetics, political science, and climatology, with postdoctoral projects on the theory of representation learning and AI for dynamics and control.

name: Luke O'Connor
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: His lab focuses on the genetic architecture of common disease, statistical methods development, and the problem of translating genetic associations into biological insight. Previously a Schmidt Fellow/PI at the Broad Institute.

name: Maha Farhat
title: Gilbert S. Omenn Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Physician-scientist and practicing pulmonary and critical care physician at Massachusetts General Hospital whose research spans microbial genomics, evolutionary genetics, AI, and clinical decision making. Associate Director of the Bioinformatics and Integrative Genomics PhD track.

name: Marinka Zitnik
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Investigates machine learning focused on geometric deep learning, multimodal learning, knowledge graphs, foundation models, and biomedical AI. Aims to lay foundations for AI that contributes to scientific understanding of medicine and therapeutic design.

name: Martin Wattenberg
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Professor at Harvard with a part-time position at Google DeepMind, currently working to understand AI systems with the goal of making them work better for people, via the Insight & Interaction Lab. Earlier work spans machine learning, data visualization, and art.

name: Melanie Weber
title: Assistant Professor of Applied Mathematics and of Computer Science
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Geometric Machine Learning Group, focusing on utilizing geometric structure in data for the design of efficient machine learning methods, with recent work on symmetry in scientific machine learning and Ricci curvature of data.

name: Michael Albergo
title: Incoming Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Junior Fellow, Harvard Society of Fellows
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies machine learning and numerical analysis methods to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences and complex systems. Uses statistical physics perspectives to understand the mechanisms underlying generative modeling.

name: Michael Baym
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Research centers on the problem of antibiotic resistance, at the intersection of experimental, theoretical, and computational techniques. Work ranges from basic mechanisms of evolution to algorithms for computation on massive biological datasets.

name: Milind Tambe
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Directs the Teamcore group, focused on advancing AI and multiagent systems research for social impact in public health, conservation, and public safety and security, often building decision aids to optimize limited intervention resources. Also Principal Scientist and Director of 'AI for Social Good' at Google Research.

name: Nada Amin
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Works at the intersection of programming languages and artificial intelligence, building intelligent systems that are correct by construction. Combines large language models with program verifiers to enable large-scale generation of verified programs.

name: Nils Gehlenborg
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops computational techniques and interfaces that enable scientists and clinicians to efficiently interact with biomedical data, tightly integrating biomedical informatics algorithms with advanced data visualization. Leads the HIDIVE Lab and directs the MMSc in Biomedical Informatics program.

name: Patrick Slade
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Bioengineering
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: His lab combines biomechanics and human-centered AI to understand and improve mobility. Uncovers causal links between cognition and motor control using neuroscience studies of human movement and develops AI techniques that encapsulate this neural and biomechanical behavior.

name: Paul Avillach
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Focuses on novel methods for integrating heterogeneous clinical cohorts, electronic health records data, and multiple types of genomics data. PI and co-investigator on large projects including the BD2K PIC-SURE Center of Excellence.

name: Pavlos Protopapas
title: Scientific Program Director and Lecturer
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include artificial intelligence, computational and data science, and modeling physical and biological phenomena and systems.

name: Peter Park
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Director, Bioinformatics and Integrative Genomics PhD Track
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: His research group specializes in computational and statistical analysis of large-scale DNA sequencing data to understand genetic and epigenetic mechanisms related to disease processes.

name: Pranav Rajpurkar
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Builds reliable artificial intelligence technologies for biomedical decision making, developing AI algorithms, datasets, and interfaces across computer vision, natural language processing, and structured health data. Has collaborated with clinicians on some of the first demonstrations of expert-level deep learning algorithms in medicine.

name: Qianqian Wang
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Her research lies at the intersection of computer vision, machine learning, and robotics, with the long-term goal of building intelligent systems that can perceive, understand, and continually learn from the physical world. Her work received the ICCV 2023 Best Student Paper Award and CVPR Best Paper Honorable Mentions in 2023 and 2025.

name: Samuel Gershman
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Psychology and Brain Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies how richly structured knowledge about the environment is acquired and how this knowledge aids adaptive behavior. His lab combines behavioral, neuroimaging, and computational techniques.

name: Sham Kakade
title: Rampell Family Professor of Computer Science and Professor of Statistics
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on advancing the fundamental capabilities needed to develop artificial general intelligence, including full-stack training pipelines for foundation models, the mathematical principles governing large-scale learning systems (emergent capabilities and scaling laws), and autonomous agent architectures.

name: Shamil Sunyaev
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Professor of Medicine, Brigham and Women's Hospital
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Computational genomicist studying population genetic variation, including the origin of mutations, effects of allelic variants on molecular function, and the genetics of human complex and Mendelian traits. Developed several computational and statistical methods widely adopted by the community.

name: Sitan Chen
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Studies algorithmic questions about learning from data, with recent work on the mathematical foundations of diffusion-based generative modeling and a theory of learning in quantum systems. Associate Faculty at the Kempner Institute and member of Harvard's ML Foundations group.

name: Stephanie Gil
title: John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Engineering and Applied Sciences
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Directs the REACT Lab (Robotics, Embedded Autonomy & Communication Theory), whose work includes reinforcement learning-based frameworks for autonomous sensing robots, trust in multiagent systems, and resilient communication for robot teams.

name: Stratos Idreos
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Data Systems Laboratory (DASlab), which designs systems that design systems for the AI era: System Calculators that automatically invent, design, and implement data and AI systems meeting tailored workload, cost, and performance targets.

name: Stuart M. Shieber
title: James O. Welch, Jr. and Virginia B. Welch Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Computer scientist whose primary research area is computational linguistics, the study of natural language from the standpoint of computer science, synthesizing knowledge from linguistics, theoretical computer science, and related fields, including work on the computational properties of grammar formalisms.

name: SueYeon Chung
title: Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Physics and of Applied Mathematics
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Explores fundamental principles of neural computation in biological and artificial neural networks, integrating neuroscience, machine learning, and statistical physics. Develops theoretical frameworks modeling the geometry and dynamics of neural population activity.

name: Susan A Murphy
title: Mallinckrodt Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
bio: Leads the Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab, which develops data-analytic algorithms and methods for informing sequential decision-making in health, including individualized adaptive interventions and micro-randomized trials.

name: Susan Murphy
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Mallinckrodt Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Leads the Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab, developing data-analytic algorithms for sequential decision making in health. Work includes just-in-time adaptive interventions delivered by smart devices.

name: Talia Konkle
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Psychology
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies how humans see and make sense of the visual world, focusing on vision, brain organization, and representation learning. Uses a combination of computational, behavioral, and neuroimaging approaches.

name: Tianxi Cai
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; John Rock Professor of Population and Translational Data Sciences, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops novel statistical and machine learning methods for mining electronic health record data, clinical trials, real-world evidence, and personalized medicine. Directs the Translational Data Science Center for a Learning Health System (CELEHS).

name: Todd Zickler
title: William and Ami Kuan Danoff Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His group works to improve the understanding of vision by making things that can see, modeling interactions between shape, light, and materials at the intersections of computer vision, graphics, machine learning, applied optics, and biological vision, motivated by robotics and augmented reality.

name: Venkatesh Murthy
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Raymond Leo Erikson Life Sciences Professor
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Interested in the neural and algorithmic basis of complex sensory-guided behaviors in terrestrial animals. His lab develops naturalistic behavioral tasks in mice combined with electrophysiological recordings.

name: Vijay Janapa Reddi
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Gordon McKay Professor at Harvard SEAS (on sabbatical at ETH Zurich) researching physical AI systems, machine learning systems, and edge computing.

name: Yannai A. Gonczarowski
title: Assistant Professor of Economics and of Computer Science
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include economics and computation, machine learning, theory of computation, and artificial intelligence.

name: Yiling Chen
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Member of Harvard's EconCS research group and faculty affiliate of the Center for Research on Computation and Society, working at the interface of economics and computation with ties to AI and theory of computation.

name: Yilun Du
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Develops generative models for reasoning, planning, embodied intelligence, and multi-agent systems, composing energy-based, diffusion, and world models to solve tasks beyond the training distribution. Leads the Embodied Minds Lab at Harvard's Kempner Institute.

name: Yue M. Lu
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Applied Mathematics
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Develops mathematical foundations for high-dimensional learning and inference, studying the principles that govern modern data-driven and AI systems using high-dimensional probability, random matrix theory, statistics, signal processing, and information theory.

name: Aleksander Mądry
title: Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, and theory of computation.

name: Alex Rives
title: Arthur Conner Career Development Professor, Assistant Professor
bio: Develops AI systems for biology; founded and led the ESM project at Meta AI that built the first large transformer language models for proteins, with applications from antibody design to modeling cellular systems.

name: Alexander (Sasha) Rakhlin
title: Professor, MIT Statistics and Data Science Center, IDSS; Department of Brain & Cognitive Sciences; Laboratory for Information & Decision Systems
department: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS) / Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: His research group works at the interface of machine learning, statistics, and optimization, formalizing the process of learning and developing tools for online prediction, decision-making, and reinforcement learning. Recent interests include neural networks, overparametrized models, and large language models.

name: Alexandru Damian
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment: Math and EECS
bio: Research focuses on the mathematical foundations of deep learning; joins MIT with a shared appointment between Mathematics and EECS.

name: Amy E. Keating
title: Jay A. Stein (1968) Professor of Biology; Professor of Biological Engineering; Department Head
bio: Determines how proteins make specific interactions with one another and designs new synthetic protein-protein interactions. Her lab integrates high-throughput assays, structural modeling, and bioinformatics with biochemical and biophysical experiments.

name: Ankur Moitra
title: Associate Director of the Institute for Data Systems & Society; Norbert Wiener Professor of Mathematics; joint appointment in EECS
bio: Theoretical computer scientist whose central goal is algorithms with provable guarantees for problems in machine learning.

name: Antonio Torralba
title: Faculty Head, AI+D; Delta Electronics Professor
bio: Faculty head of the AI+D track at MIT EECS; research areas include machine learning and vision and graphics.

name: Armando Solar-Lezama
title: Distinguished Professor of Computing, MIT Schwarzman College of Computing; Professor of EECS
bio: Leads the Computer-Aided Programming Group, developing program synthesis techniques for reliable software and reframing traditional machine learning problems as program synthesis.

name: Arvind Satyanarayan
title: Associate Professor
bio: Leads the MIT Visualization Group, using interactive data visualization to study intelligence augmentation: how computational systems can amplify cognition and creativity while respecting agency.

name: Ashia Wilson
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, and theory of computation.

name: Asu Ozdaglar
title: EECS Department Head; MIT Schwarzman College of Computing Deputy Dean of Academics; MathWorks Professor
bio: Research spans optimization, machine learning, economics, game theory, and networks; recent focus includes game-theoretic AI, multi-agent decision-making and reinforcement learning, and human-AI collaboration.

name: Bailey Flanigan
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment with Political Science, Theodore T. Miller (1922) Career Development Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, optimization and game theory, and theory of computation, with a shared appointment in Political Science.

name: Bonnie Berger
title: Simons Professor of Mathematics; Head, Computation and Biology Group, CSAIL
bio: A pioneer of computational molecular biology, she designs algorithms to gain biological insights from large automated data sets, working on compressive genomics, network inference, structural bioinformatics, genomic privacy, and medical genomics. She heads the Computation and Biology group at MIT CSAIL.

name: Caroline Uhler
title: Andrew (1956) and Erna Viterbi Professor; Professor of EECS and in IDSS
bio: Her lab develops machine learning foundations for integrating data modalities and inferring causal relationships, applied to discovering the regulatory circuits of cells and tissues in health and disease.

name: Cheng Zhi (Anna) Huang
title: Robert N. Noyce Career Development Professor, Associate Professor (shared appointment, Music and Theater Arts and EECS)
bio: Holds a shared appointment between Music and Theater Arts and EECS; her work centers on AI and music technology, including human-AI resonance in music making.

name: Collin Stultz
title: Nina T. and Robert H. Rubin Professor; Co-Director, Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology (HST); Associate Director, Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES)
bio: Co-Director of the Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology; research areas include AI for healthcare and life sciences and biomedical systems.

name: Connor Coley
title: Class of 1957 Career Development Professor; Associate Professor of Chemical Engineering (shared appointment in EECS)
bio: His group develops computational methods at the intersection of artificial intelligence and chemistry, with relevance to small-molecule drug discovery, chemical synthesis, and structure elucidation. Interests include autonomous discovery, laboratory automation, and molecular design.

name: Connor Wilson Coley
title: Associate Professor / Shared appointment in ChemE
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and biomedical systems, with a shared appointment in Chemical Engineering.

name: Constantinos Daskalakis
title: Armen Avanessians (1982) Professor
bio: Works on computation theory and its interface with game theory, economics, probability, statistics, and machine learning.

name: Dan Huttenlocher
title: Dean, MIT Schwarzman College of Computing; Henry Ellis Warren (1894) Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Chair, MIT Jameel Clinic
bio: Inaugural dean of the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing and chair of the Jameel Clinic. He previously helped found Cornell Tech and served as its first Dean and Vice Provost, with a mixed academic and industry background including Xerox PARC.

name: Daniel Huttenlocher
title: Dean, MIT Stephen A. Schwarzman College of Computing; Panasonic Professor
bio: Dean of the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing; recent work examines the broader implications of AI, including co-authoring the book The Age of AI: And Our Human Future.

name: Daniela Rus
title: Director, CSAIL; Panasonic Professor
bio: Director of CSAIL; research interests are in robotics, mobile computing, and data science, including machine learning algorithms for robust control of autonomous vehicles.

name: David Alexander Bruns-Smith
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment with MIT Sloan School of Management
bio: Works on machine learning methods for causal inference, including debiased machine learning for instrumental variables and reinforcement learning, applied to macroeconomics and household finance.

name: David Sontag
title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / CSAIL / IMES
bio: Leads the Clinical Machine Learning Group at MIT, focusing on advancing machine learning and artificial intelligence and using them to transform health care. He is affiliated with IMES, CSAIL, and the Jameel Clinic.

name: Devavrat Shah
title: Andrew (1956) and Erna Viterbi Professor
bio: Research focuses on social data processing and practical algorithms for statistical inference, with long-standing interests in distributed network algorithms and network information theory.

name: Dimitris Bertsimas
title: Associate Dean of Business Analytics; Boeing Professor of Operations Research
department: MIT Sloan School of Management (Operations Research)
bio: His research focuses on optimization, machine learning, and applied probability, with applications in healthcare, finance, operations management, and transportation. He is the Entrepreneurship faculty lead of the MIT Jameel Clinic.

name: Dina Katabi
title: Thuan (1990) and Nicole Pham Professor
bio: Research spans digital health, wireless sensors, mobile computing, machine learning, and computer vision.

name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and robotics.

name: Elazer Edelman
title: Edward J. Poitras Professor in Medical Engineering and Science; Director, Institute for Medical Engineering and Science
department: Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES)
bio: A physician-scientist whose laboratory has pioneered basic findings in vascular biology and the development and assessment of biotechnology. He directs MIT's IMES and Clinical Research Center and is a senior attending physician at Brigham and Women's Hospital.

name: Elfar Adalsteinsson
title: Eaton-Peabody Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI for healthcare, biomedical systems, and vision and graphics.

name: Fotini Christia
title: Ford International Professor of the Social Sciences; Director, Sociotechnical Systems Research Center
bio: A political scientist who directs MIT's Sociotechnical Systems Research Center and is Associate Director of IDSS, chairing the Social and Engineering Systems doctoral program in the Schwarzman College of Computing. She works to bridge the social sciences, data science, and computation.

name: Frederic Durand
title: Amar Bose Professor
bio: Research spans picture generation and creation, including realistic graphics, real-time rendering, and computational photography, drawing on signal processing and perceptual science.

name: Gabriele Farina
title: X-Window Consortium Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and optimization and game theory.

name: Georgia Perakis
title: John C Head III Dean (Interim), MIT Sloan School of Management; Professor of Operations Management, Operations Research and Statistics
bio: Her research sits at the intersection of optimization and machine learning, with applications in pricing, revenue management, supply chain, and healthcare. She has been on the MIT Sloan faculty since 1998 and is a Jameel Clinic Principal Investigator.

name: Gregory Wornell
title: Sumitomo Electric Industries Professor in Engineering
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, communications, vision and graphics, and information and decision systems.

name: Guy Bresler
title: Education Officer for AI+D; Professor of EECS and in IDSS
bio: Works at the interface of information theory, statistics, theoretical computer science, and probability, studying the computational tractability of high-dimensional inference.

name: Hal Abelson
title: Class of 1922 Professor
bio: Works on democratizing computing, making information technology a tool for everyone from schoolchildren to policymakers; also active in internet policy research at CSAIL.

name: Jacob Andreas
title: ITT Career Development Professor in Computer Technology; Associate Professor of EECS
bio: Studies language as a communicative and computational tool, building machine learning models that learn language and use it to reason about the world.

name: James DiCarlo
title: Peter de Florez Professor of Brain and Cognitive Sciences; Director, MIT Quest for Intelligence; Investigator, McGovern Institute
department: Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences / McGovern Institute
bio: His goal is to reverse engineer the brain mechanisms underlying human visual intelligence, combining large-scale neurophysiology, brain imaging, neural perturbation, and machine learning to build neurally mechanistic models of the ventral visual stream. This work aims to enable new artificial vision and AI approaches and brain-machine interfaces.

name: James J. Collins
title: Termeer Professor of Medical Engineering & Science; Professor of Biological Engineering; Life Sciences Faculty Lead, MIT Jameel Clinic
department: Department of Biological Engineering / Institute for Medical Engineering & Science
bio: His group works in synthetic and systems biology, using network biology and AI approaches to study antibiotic action, bacterial defense mechanisms, and the emergence of resistance. He directs the Antibiotics-AI Project at MIT and is a founding faculty member of the Wyss Institute.

name: Joel Voldman
title: William R. Brody (1965) Professor
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / Research Laboratory of Electronics

title: Gilbert Helman Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches statistics, optimization, reinforcement learning, machine learning theory, and information theory. Holds a secondary appointment in Electrical and Systems Engineering.

name: Zachary Ives
title: Adani President's Distinguished Professor and Department Chair
bio: Adani President's Distinguished Professor and chair of Penn CIS, working on data integration, data provenance and trustworthiness, and machine learning systems. Affiliated with the ASSET Center for Safe, Explainable and Trustworthy AI and the Warren Center.

name: Zhimei Ren
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on distribution-free inference, multiple hypothesis testing, data-driven decision making, causal inference, and survival analysis.

name: Aaron Newman
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science
bio: His group combines computational and experimental techniques to study the cellular organization of complex tissues, focusing on the phenotypic diversity and clinical significance of tumor cell subsets and their surrounding microenvironments, and develops innovative data science tools.

name: Akshay Chaudhari
title: Associate Professor of Radiology and of Biomedical Data Science; Interim Division Chief, Integrative Biomedical Imaging Informatics at Stanford
bio: Interested in applying artificial intelligence to all aspects of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, quantitative analysis, clinical decision support, and prediction of patient outcomes. Develops self-supervised and representation learning techniques for multimodal deep learning in healthcare using vision, language, and medical-records data.

name: Alex Ioannidis
title: Assistant Professor of Genetics and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Research focuses on the design of algorithms and application of computational methods for problems in precision health, genomics, clinical data science, and AI in healthcare. He earned his PhD from Stanford in Computational and Mathematical Engineering.

name: Andrew Gentles
title: Associate Professor (Research) of Pathology, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Works on computational systems biology, with research appointments in Pathology, Computational Medicine, and by courtesy in Biomedical Data Science.

name: Anshul Kundaje
title: Associate Professor of Genetics and of Computer Science
bio: The Kundaje lab develops machine learning models of gene regulation to decipher the genetic and molecular basis of disease, pioneering deep learning models and interpretation frameworks to decode the functional language of DNA, RNA, and proteins. He has led computational efforts of large genomics consortia including the ENCODE Project.

name: Azalia Mirhoseini
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Directs the Scaling Intelligence lab, focused on developing scalable and self-improving AI systems. Her past work includes Mixture-of-Experts neural architectures, AlphaChip (an RL approach to chip layout used for Google TPUs), and pioneering research on LLM test-time scaling at Google Brain, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.

name: Barbara Engelhardt
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Develops and applies models for structured biomedical data that capture patterns, predict results of interventions, assist with decision-making support, and prioritize experiments. She is also a Senior Investigator at Gladstone Institutes.

name: Brandon Westover
title: Professor of Neurology and Neurological Sciences (Adult Neurology) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science and of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
department: Department of Neurology and Neurological Sciences
bio: Epilepsy specialist, clinical neurophysiologist, and director of the Stanford Epilepsy Center whose research develops artificial intelligence technology to protect and improve brain health. His interests include predicting seizures and detecting and forecasting disorders of memory, cognition, and consciousness such as delirium and coma.

name: Brian Hie
title: Assistant Professor of Chemical Engineering; Dieter Schwarz Foundation Stanford Data Science Faculty Fellow
bio: Supervises the Laboratory of Evolutionary Design, conducting research at the intersection of biology and machine learning. He is also an Innovation Investigator at the Arc Institute and an HAI Faculty Affiliate.

name: C. Karen Liu
title: Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research interests span computer graphics and robotics, including physics-based animation, character animation, optimal control, reinforcement learning, and computational biomechanics. She develops computational approaches to modeling realistic human movement and learning control policies for humanoids and assistive robots.

name: Carlos Guestrin
title: Fortinet Founders Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Previously the Amazon Professor of Machine Learning at the University of Washington and Senior Director of Machine Learning and AI at Apple after the acquisition of Turi, which he co-founded. His team released popular open-source ML projects including XGBoost, LIME, Apache TVM, and MXNet.

name: Chelsea Finn
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
bio: Her research enables robots and other agents to develop broadly intelligent behavior through learning and interaction, at the intersection of machine learning and robotic control. Topics include end-to-end learning of visual perception and manipulation, deep reinforcement learning from autonomously collected data, and meta-learning.

name: Chiara Sabatti
title: Professor, Department of Biomedical Data Science and of Statistics; Associate Chair of Education & Training
bio: Develops statistical approaches for high-dimensional data to improve understanding of the genetic basis of human health-related traits. She is a Senior Fellow at Stanford HAI and Associate Director of Stanford Data Science.

name: Christopher Manning
title: Thomas M. Siebel Professor of Machine Learning, Professor of Linguistics and of Computer Science, and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Director of the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (SAIL) and Associate Director of Stanford HAI. From 2010 he pioneered natural language understanding and inference using deep learning, with impactful research including the GloVe word vectors, attention, neural machine translation, and question answering.

name: Christopher Re
title: Professor of Computer Science
bio: Member of the Stanford AI Lab, affiliated with the Machine Learning Group and the Center for Research on Foundation Models. His recent work examines how software and hardware systems will change because of machine learning; research from his group contributed to Evo, a DNA foundation model, and is used in products at Apple, Google, and YouTube.

name: Curtis Langlotz
title: Professor of Radiology, of Medicine and of Biomedical Data Science; Senior Associate Vice Provost for Research
bio: His laboratory investigates the use of deep neural networks and other machine learning technologies to detect disease and eliminate diagnostic errors through analysis of medical images and clinical notes, including multimodal contrastive learning with radiology reports.

name: Dan Jurafsky
title: Reynolds Professor in Humanities, Professor of Linguistics and Professor of Computer Science
bio: Co-author of the widely used textbook 'Speech and Language Processing' and recipient of a 2002 MacArthur Fellowship. His research ranges across computational linguistics, with special interests in natural language understanding and human-human conversation.

name: Daniel Ho
title: William Benjamin Scott & Luna M. Scott Professor of Law, Professor of Political Science, and Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Stanford Law School; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Directs Stanford's Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab (RegLab) and is a Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI. He has served on the National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Commission (NAIAC), advising the White House on artificial intelligence.

name: Daniel Yamins
title: Associate Professor of Psychology and of Computer Science
bio: Leads the NeuroAILab, whose research lies at the intersection of neuroscience, artificial intelligence, psychology, and large-scale data analysis. The lab studies how the brain solves computational challenges in order to build better AI systems.

name: Dennis Wall
title: Professor of Pediatrics (Systems Medicine), of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences; Director of Graduate Studies (PhD)
bio: Runs a lab in pediatric innovation focused on biomedical informatics methods to disentangle complex conditions that originate in childhood, including autism and related developmental delays. His work targets systems biology for the design of clinical solutions that detect and treat disease.

name: Diyi Yang
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research interests are computational social science and natural language processing, aiming to understand the social aspects of language and build socially aware NLP systems to better support human-human and human-computer interaction. Recipient of a Microsoft Research Faculty Fellowship and NSF CAREER Award.

name: Dora Demszky
title: Assistant Professor, Graduate School of Education and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Graduate School of Education; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Develops natural language processing methods to support equitable and student-centered instruction. Her tools give teachers feedback on dialogic instructional practices and analyze representation in textbooks.

name: Dorsa Sadigh
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, of Electrical Engineering, and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Her research includes planning for autonomous cars that coordinate with people, leveraging effects on human actions for planning and active information gathering over human internal state. She is a member of the Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute and Human Performance Alliance.

name: Edward Chang
title: Adjunct Professor, Computer Science
bio: A pioneer in data-centric parallel machine learning since 2005, he serves as CTO of AILLY.ai and was previously president of HTC Healthcare (DeepQ) and a director of research at Google leading scalable machine learning and recommendation systems. Recipient of the NSF CAREER award and a $1M Tricorder XPRIZE for AI-based disease diagnosis.

name: Ehsan Adeli
title: Assistant Professor of Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science and of Computer Science; Director, Stanford Translational AI (STAI) Lab
department: Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Directs the Stanford Translational AI (STAI) Lab, developing translational AI algorithms for medicine and mental health. His work analyzes human activities from video and brain MRIs with explainable machine learning to study neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric diseases.

name: Ellen Vitercik
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering and of Computer Science
department: Management Science and Engineering and Computer Science
bio: Assistant Professor in Management Science and Engineering and Computer Science; her courses include AI for Algorithmic Reasoning and Optimization and Design and Analysis of Algorithms.

name: Emily Alsentzer
title: Assistant Professor in Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, Computer Science
bio: Leverages machine learning and natural language processing to augment clinical decision-making and broaden access to high-quality healthcare. Focuses on integrating medical expertise into ML models to ensure responsible deployment in clinical workflows.

name: Emily Fox
title: Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
bio: Professor in the Departments of Statistics and Computer Science; previously the Amazon Professor of Machine Learning at the University of Washington. From 2018-2021 she led the Health AI team at Apple as a Distinguished Engineer.

name: Emma Brunskill
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research develops reinforcement learning and contextual bandit methods for personalized decision making, including interventions in mobile health and online education. She teaches Stanford's Reinforcement Learning course (CS 234).

name: Emma Lundberg
title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering and of Pathology
bio: At the intersection of bioimaging, proteomics, and artificial intelligence, her research aims to define the spatiotemporal organization of the human proteome at cellular and subcellular levels. She directs the Cell Atlas of the Human Protein Atlas and works toward virtual cell models that simulate cell behavior.

name: Euan A. Ashley
title: Roger and Joelle Burnell Professor of Genomics and Precision Health; Professor of Medicine (Cardiovascular Medicine), of Genetics and of Biomedical Data Science; Associate Dean, School of Medicine
bio: The Ashley lab focuses on precision medicine, developing methods for the interpretation of whole-genome sequencing data to improve diagnosis of genetic disease and personalize the practice of medicine. The lab embraces big data questions and systems approaches to biology, including analysis of network graphs.

name: Fei-Fei Li
title: Sequoia Capital Professor, Senior Fellow at HAI, and Professor, by courtesy, of Operations, Information and Technology at the Graduate School of Business
bio: Founding Co-Director of Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute and Director of Stanford's AI Lab from 2013 to 2018. She served as VP at Google and Chief Scientist of AI/ML at Google Cloud, and is Co-founder/CEO of World Labs, an AI company focusing on spatial intelligence and generative AI.

name: Gregory Valiant
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Works on algorithms, machine learning, statistics, and information theory. A main theme of his work is designing efficient algorithms for accurately inferring information about complex distributions given limited data or constraints on computation, memory, or data quality.

name: Hariharan Subramonyam
title: Assistant Professor (Research) of Education and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Graduate School of Education; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Faculty Fellow at Stanford HAI and member of the Stanford HCI Group. His research augments critical human tasks such as learning, creativity, and sensemaking with AI, drawing on cognitive psychology, and studies tools for multidisciplinary teams to co-design AI experiences.

name: James Landay
title: Denning Co-Director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, Anand Rajaraman and Venky Harinarayan Professor, and Professor of Computer Science
bio: Specializes in human-computer interaction and is co-founder and Co-Director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Previously a professor at Cornell Tech and the University of Washington, and Director of Intel Labs Seattle.

name: James Zou
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Biomedical Data Science; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Works on making machine learning more reliable, human-compatible, and statistically rigorous, with particular interest in applications to human disease and health. Part of the Stanford AI Lab and a Chan-Zuckerberg Investigator.

name: Jason Fries
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Medicine (Computational Medicine)
bio: Research focuses on training and evaluating foundation models for healthcare, positioned at the intersection of computer science, medical informatics, and hospital systems. Explores the use of electronic health record data to contextualize human health, leveraging longitudinal patient information for model development.

name: Jeannette Bohg
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research focuses on perception and learning for autonomous robotic manipulation and grasping. She develops goal-directed, real-time, multi-modal methods, building on earlier work in multi-modal scene understanding for robotic grasping.

name: Jiajun Wu
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and, by courtesy, of Psychology
bio: Works on computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and computational cognitive science. His research has been recognized with the IJCAI Computers and Thought Award, an NSF CAREER award, and dissertation awards from ACM and AAAI.

name: Jonathan H. Chen
title: Assistant Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine)
bio: Leads a research group combining human and artificial intelligence approaches to deliver better care than either alone. Taps real-world clinical data streams like electronic medical records with machine learning and data analytics to produce reproducible clinical decision support.

name: Julia Palacios
title: Associate Professor of Statistics, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Biology
bio: Her research spans Bayesian nonparametrics, probabilistic AI, stochastic processes, and computational statistics. Her group develops stochastic models and efficient inference algorithms for understanding evolutionary dynamics in population genetics, infectious diseases and cancer.

name: Julia Salzman
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science, of Biochemistry and, by courtesy, of Statistics
bio: Her lab views genomic data as a statistical signal processing problem, leveraging tools from statistics, traditional machine learning and deep learning for biological discovery. The lab introduced SPLASH, a unifying reference-genome-agnostic paradigm for sequence analysis, with focus areas in splicing, cancer and microbes.

name: Jure Leskovec
title: Alfred and Rebecca Lin Professor of Computer Science
bio: Affiliated with the Stanford AI Lab, Machine Learning Group, and Center for Research on Foundation Models; he pioneered the field of Graph Neural Networks and co-authored PyG, the most widely used GNN library. He served as Chief Scientist at Pinterest and an investigator at Chan Zuckerberg BioHub.

name: Kayvon Fatahalian
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: His research focuses on the design of systems for real-time graphics, high-efficiency simulation engines for applications in entertainment and AI, and platforms for analyzing images and videos at scale.

name: Kunle Olukotun
title: Cadence Design Systems Professor, Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Computer Science
bio: A pioneer in multicore processor design and leader of the Stanford Hydra chip multiprocessor project; in 2017 he co-founded SambaNova Systems, a machine learning and AI company, where he serves as Chief Technologist. He directs the Pervasive Parallel Lab and is a member of the DAWN Lab, developing infrastructure for usable machine learning.

name: Leila Wehbe
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Neurology and Neurological Sciences (Adult Neurology)

name: Leonidas Guibas
title: Paul Pigott Professor of Engineering and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: Heads the Geometric Computation group and is a member of Stanford's Computer Graphics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratories. He works on algorithms for sensing, modeling, reasoning, rendering, and acting on the physical world, including geometric modeling with point clouds and 3D shape libraries.

name: Lu Tian
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Statistics; Director of Graduate Studies (MS)
bio: Research interests include survival analysis and semiparametric modeling, resampling methods, meta-analysis, high-dimensional data analysis, and precision medicine for disease diagnosis, prognosis and treatment.

name: Mark Musen
title: Stanford Medicine Professor of Computational Medicine; Professor of Medicine and of Biomedical Data Science; Chief, Division of Computational Medicine
bio: Conducts research on open science, data stewardship, intelligent systems, and biomedical decision support. His laboratory studies semantic technology in a range of application systems, emphasizing approaches that enhance the stewardship and dissemination of experimental data.

name: Matthew Lungren
title: Adjunct Professor, Biomedical Data Science
bio: Physician-scientist whose research develops and evaluates machine learning systems that combine medical imaging, electronic health record data, and clinical outcomes. Current work concerns medical foundation models, agentic clinical systems, and the prospective evaluation of AI in real clinical workflows.

name: Mehran Sahami
title: Tencent Chair of the Computer Science Department and James and Ellenor Chesebrough Professor
bio: Professor (Teaching) in Computer Science and a Bass Fellow in Undergraduate Education; before Stanford he was a Senior Research Scientist at Google. His research interests include computer science education, artificial intelligence, and ethics.

name: Michael Bernstein
title: Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Focuses on designing social, societal, and interactive technologies. He is a Bass University Fellow and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence.

name: Michael Genesereth
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Known for his work on computational logic and its applications in enterprise management, computational law, and general game playing. He directs the Logic Group at Stanford and is founder and research director of CodeX, the Stanford Center for Legal Informatics.

name: Michael Snyder
title: Stanford W. Ascherman Professor of Genetics; Director, Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine
bio: Directs the Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine; his laboratory uses a variety of large-scale omics approaches to analyze genomes, transcriptomes and regulatory networks in yeast and humans.

name: Mirabela Rusu
title: Assistant Professor of Radiology (Integrative Biomedical Imaging Informatics) and, by courtesy, of Urology and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Leads the Personalized Integrative Medicine Laboratory (PIMed), developing analytic methods for biomedical data integration with a particular interest in radiology-pathology fusion to create multi-scale representations of pathological conditions.

name: Monica Lam
title: Kleiner Perkins, Mayfield, Sequoia Capital Professor in the School of Engineering, Professor of Computer Science and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: Her current research is creating effective and reliable AI assistants to accelerate the discovery of knowledge. Her OVAL lab has created open-source LLM-based tools used by consumers, historians, and journalists, including the STORM deep-research agent used by about a million users.

name: Nigam H. Shah
title: Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and of Biomedical Data Science; Chief Data Scientist, Stanford Health Care
bio: His research group analyzes multiple types of health data — EHR, claims, wearables, weblogs, and patient blogs — to answer clinical questions, generate insights, and build predictive models for the learning health system.

name: Nima Aghaeepour
title: Professor of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine, of Pediatrics and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
bio: Machine learning and artificial intelligence scientist whose laboratory develops computational methods to study clinical and biological modalities in translational settings. Focuses on leveraging multiomics studies, wearable devices, and electronic health records to address clinical challenges in perioperative care and maternal and child health.

name: Noah Goodman
title: Professor of Psychology and of Computer Science
bio: Professor of Psychology and Computer Science and HAI faculty affiliate studying probabilistic models of cognition and language. His group's work spans probabilistic programming approaches to affective computing and rational models of communication, including polite language use and theory of mind.

name: Olivier Gevaert
title: Associate Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: His lab focuses on biomedical data fusion: developing machine learning methods for biomedical decision support using multi-scale biomedical data. Previous work pioneered Bayesian and kernel data-fusion methods in breast and ovarian cancer and algorithms for identifying cancer driver genes.

name: Oussama Khatib
title: Weichai Professor and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: His robotics research covers novel control architectures, algorithms, sensing, and human-friendly designs that enable robots to interact cooperatively and safely with humans and the physical world. Applications span healthcare, industry, agriculture, and dangerous or unreachable settings such as deep oceans, mines, and space.

name: Percy Liang
title: Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Director of the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM), focused on making foundation models more accessible through open source and understandable through rigorous benchmarking. His past work spans machine learning and NLP, including robustness, interpretability, semantics, and reasoning.

name: Robert Tibshirani
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Statistics
bio: Works in applied statistics, biostatistics, and data mining, specializing in computer-intensive methods for regression and classification, bootstrap, cross-validation and statistical inference, and signal and image analysis for medical diagnosis. Co-author of 'The Elements of Statistical Learning' and 'An Introduction to the Bootstrap'.

name: Ron Dror
title: Cheriton Family Professor and Professor, by courtesy, of Structural Biology and of Molecular & Cellular Physiology
bio: Leads a Stanford AI Lab research group that uses molecular simulation and machine learning to elucidate biomolecular structure, dynamics, and function, and to guide development of more effective medicines. Previously served as second-in-command of D. E. Shaw Research.

name: Roxana Daneshjou
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Dermatology
bio: Physician-scientist with an MD and a PhD in Genetics who completed a postdoc in Biomedical Data Science with James Zou. She is assistant director of the Center of Excellence for Precision Health & Pharmacogenomics, director of informatics for the Stanford Skin Innovation and Interventional Research Group, and a faculty affiliate of Stanford HAI and the AI in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI) center.

name: Russ B. Altman
title: Kenneth Fong Professor and Professor of Bioengineering, of Genetics, of Medicine, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Applies computing and AI/data science to problems in molecular biology of relevance to medicine, focusing on drug response at the molecular level. His laboratory builds the PharmGKB pharmacogenomics knowledge base relating genetic variation to variation in drug response.

name: Sanmi Koyejo
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Leads the Stanford Trustworthy AI Research (STAIR) lab, developing measurement-theoretic foundations for trustworthy AI spanning AI evaluation science, algorithmic accountability, and privacy-preserving machine learning. Applications include healthcare and scientific discovery; his AI evaluation work was cited in the 2024 Economic Report of the President.

name: Scott Linderman
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics; Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute; Co-Director, Stanford Center for Neural Data Science
bio: His research focuses on machine learning, computational neuroscience, and how computational and statistical methods can help decipher neural computation. He combines methodological development in state space models, deep generative models, and approximate Bayesian inference with applied analyses of large-scale neural and behavioral data.

name: Serena Yeung-Levy
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
bio: Develops artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to enable new capabilities in biomedicine and healthcare, with expertise in deep learning and computer vision applied to video of human behavior, medical images, and cell microscopy images. She leads the Medical AI and Computer Vision Lab at Stanford and is a Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Investigator.

name: Shuran Song
title: Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Her research lies at the intersection of computer vision and robotics. Her work has been recognized with Best Paper Awards at RSS'22 and T-RO'20 and Best System Paper Awards at CoRL'21 and RSS'19, along with an NSF CAREER Award and a Sloan fellowship.

name: Stefano Ermon
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
bio: Affiliated with the Stanford AI Lab, his research centers on scalable and accurate inference in graphical models, statistical modeling of data, large-scale combinatorial optimization, and robust decision making under uncertainty. Much of his work is motivated by applications in computational sustainability.

name: Stephen B. Montgomery
title: Professor of Pathology, of Genetics, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science; Director of Admissions
bio: Studies the effects of genome variation on cellular phenotypes and disease using next-generation RNA sequencing combined with state-of-the-art bioinformatics and statistical genetics approaches. He is best known for his work mapping the effects of genetic variation on gene expression.

name: Sylvia K. Plevritis
title: Professor and Chair, Department of Biomedical Data Science; Director, Biomedical Informatics Training Program
bio: Leads a systems biology cancer research program that bridges multiomic, imaging, clinical and population data to decipher properties of cancer. Her laboratory develops stochastic models of the natural history of cancer to estimate population-level outcomes under differing screening and treatment interventions.

name: Tatsunori Hashimoto
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Uses tools from statistics to make machine learning systems more robust and trustworthy, especially complex systems such as large language models. His research uses robustness and worst-case performance as a lens on fundamental challenges in machine learning and NLP.

name: Tengyu Ma
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Recipient of a Sloan Research Fellowship, the NIPS Best Student Paper Award, and the COLT Best Paper Award. He teaches Stanford's Machine Learning course (CS 229).

name: Teri Klein
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Genetics
bio: Principal Investigator of PharmGKB, CPIC, PharmCAT and ClinGen. Her research spans pharmacogenomics, personalized medicine, computational biology and bioinformatics, including clinical dosing guidelines for pharmacogenomics and annotation of the human genome.

name: Tina Hernandez-Boussard
title: Professor of Medicine (Biomedical Informatics), of Biomedical Data Science, of Surgery and, by courtesy, of Epidemiology & Population Health; Associate Dean of Research
bio: Her work is at the intersection of informatics and population health, applying novel methods and tools to large clinical datasets for hypothesis generation, comparative effectiveness research, and the evaluation of quality healthcare delivery.

name: Vasilis Syrgkanis
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering and, by courtesy, of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
department: Management Science and Engineering; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: His courses include Foundations of Causal Machine Learning, Applied Causal Inference with Machine Learning and AI, and Game Theory, Data Science and AI. Member of the Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering (ICME).

name: Wing Hung Wong
title: Stephen R. Pierce Family Goldman Sachs Professor of Science and Human Health; Professor of Statistics and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Current research interests are Bayesian statistics, computational biology, precision medicine and semiconductor-based automation of biological experiments. His lab has contributed Monte Carlo algorithms for Bayesian computation and bioinformatics tools for microarray and sequencing data, with current work on gene regulatory analysis.

name: Yejin Choi
title: Dieter Schwarz Foundation Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: MacArthur Fellow (2022), AI2050 Senior Fellow, and named to the Time100 Most Influential People in AI in 2023. Co-recipient of two test-of-time awards and eight best/outstanding paper awards at top AI conferences including ACL, ICML, NeurIPS, ICCV, and CVPR.

name: Zihuai He
title: Assistant Professor (Research) of Neurology, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
department: Department of Neurology and Neurological Sciences
bio: Research concentrates on statistical genomics and integrative analysis of omics data, developing novel statistical and computational methods to study Alzheimer's disease and aging.
